sentences.text: Macrogryphosaurus means "big enigmatic lizard" and is an elasmarian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina.
This large ornithopod is noted for a series of mineralized thoracic plates, also called intercostal plates, located on its chest.
Its short torso, combined with a fused birdlike sternum, would have made the body rather stiff.
It stands as the largest known species of South American ornithopod, excluding Hadrosauridae, and is the biggest known elasmarian.
Researchers consider the genus important because its complete remains provide crucial information on the group's anatomy.
A complete osteology was published in 2020 by Sebastián Rozadilla, Penélope Cruzado-Caballero, and Jorge O. Calvo.
An articulated, nearly complete skeleton was discovered in May 1999 at Mari Menuco Lake by a young boy named Rafael Moyano.
Dr. Stephen F. Poropat described the fossil preservation as "amazing."
The species was formally described and named in 2007 by Jorge O. Calvo, Juan D. Porfiri, and Fernando E. Novas.
The holotype specimen MUCPv-32 includes an essentially complete set of vertebrae, ribs, four thoracic plates, pectoral girdles, and a sternum.
The holotype MUCPv-321 is estimated at 6 meters long, and likely had not reached adult size due to unfused vertebrae.
The species name gondwanicus refers to the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.
As a basal iguanodontian, it was likely a bipedal herbivore.
The dinosaur is estimated to have reached around 6 meters in length, though the known specimen may not have been fully grown.
Phylogenetic analysis links it to Talenkauen, leading Calvo and colleagues to propose the new clade Elasmaria for both genera.
It lived during the Coniacian age, approximately 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
